text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* The agreement between centre-right opposition and centre-left ruling coalition over extending television licences broke down following protests by state broadcaster RAI (all).
* Telecoms minister Antonio Maccanico says in an interview that a compromise on broadcasting regulations will be found sooner or later (La Repubblica).
* Head of employers' organisation Confindustria Giorgio Fossa launches another attack against the government on the need for a mini-budget to meet Maastricht criteria (all).
* The wife of former minister and ex-magistrate Antonio Di Pietro says in court her husbad was fed up and tired before resigning as top judge in corruption investigations (all).
* Bank of Italy's governor Antonio Fazio urges banks to lower their rates (Sole 24 Ore).
* Bonn slows down on stability pact, Ecofin ministers search for a compromise ahead of Dublin summit (Sole 24 Ore)
* Italy had a 50.06 trln trade surplus in September (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
